complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Implement plain-text conversion and search index use case
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break this task into four subtasks: (1) Create the plain-text conversion utility with comprehensive regex-based Markdown stripping (fenced blocks, HTML, links, markers, inline code, tables, whitespace), (2) Implement the GetBlogSearchIndex use case following the established UseCase pattern (see ListBlogPosts.ts as reference), (3) Create the BlogSearchEntryDTO type and update barrel exports, (4) Create the /blog/search-index.json route handler following rss.xml/route.ts as the architectural template with generateStaticParams and error handling.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This task is moderately complex (6/10) because: (1) The plain-text converter requires careful regex design to handle ~9 Markdown constructs while preserving index mapping via NFC normalization, (2) The use case follows well-established patterns (ListBlogPosts, rss.xml route) reducing cognitive load, (3) No new architectural decisions needed—repository, filters (publishedOnly, newestFirst), and error handling patterns already exist, (4) The route is greenfield but has a clear template in rss.xml/route.ts (same generateStaticParams, Response pattern, error handling), (5) Testing requires both unit tests (regex edge cases) and integration tests (route behavior). The codebase already has 15 blog use case tests and similar route patterns, making this incremental rather than exploratory work.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Create generic text utilities for search
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break this task into three subtasks: (1) Implement foldForSearch with character-by-character NFD diacritic removal while maintaining 1:1 index mapping and handling edge cases like Turkish İ and multi-code-unit characters, (2) Implement excerptAround with word-boundary detection, ellipsis logic, and offset tracking for arbitrary radius values, (3) Update package.json exports and create comprehensive test coverage for both utilities including accent handling, index preservation, boundary conditions, and radius variations.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This task is moderately-high complexity (7/10) because: (1) foldForSearch has subtle Unicode requirements—NFD normalization, preserving 1:1 character mapping, handling Turkish İ edge case where lowercase produces multiple code units—these are easy to get wrong, (2) excerptAround requires careful word-boundary detection (~radius words on each side), ellipsis placement logic (conditional on start/end), and accurate offset calculation in the original string, (3) The utilities are domain-agnostic and will be reused, so they need defensive implementation and thorough edge-case testing, (4) The codebase has @repo/utils with 20+ existing utility tests providing clear patterns (see Validator.test.ts), but this is new territory (no existing text manipulation utilities), (5) Needs package.json export configuration following the established pattern (see ./hooks, ./validator exports), (6) Testing must cover Portuguese/Spanish accents, whitespace variations, boundary conditions, and index mapping verification.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Implement client-side search logic (matching, ranking, excerpting)
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break this task into five subtasks: (1) Create the SearchablePost type and parseQuery function (trim, normalize, fold, split, filter <2 chars), (2) Implement rankPosts with AND-across-terms matching logic, field-priority ranking (title=0, tags=1, description=2, body=3), and stable sort preserving newest-first order, (3) Implement bodyExcerpt to find the first term match, call excerptAround, and map all term occurrences within the excerpt boundaries adjusting for offset, (4) Create comprehensive unit tests covering all ranking scenarios, multi-term AND logic, accent folding, tie-breaking, empty bodies, and excerpt highlighting, (5) Ensure strict browser-bundle hygiene—no @repo/application imports, only local SearchablePost type.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This task is high complexity (8/10) because: (1) rankPosts has intricate AND-across-terms logic—every term must match at least one field per post, then posts are ranked by best-matching field (0-3), with stable sort preserving original order on ties—this is easy to get wrong, (2) The logic depends on foldForSearch for case/accent-insensitive matching, requiring careful coordination between folded and original text, (3) bodyExcerpt must find the first occurrence of any term in the folded body, extract an excerpt via excerptAround, then map all term positions inside the excerpt (adjusting for offset)—three layers of index manipulation, (4) Browser-bundle constraint is critical: client components must never import @repo/application (which contains use cases, DTOs, repository interfaces)—using SearchablePost instead of BlogPostSummaryDTO is a new pattern not seen elsewhere in apps/site/src/features/, (5) Testing needs to cover edge cases: multiple terms matching different fields, ties with stable sort, missing bodies (index not loaded yet), accent variations, no-match scenarios, (6) Pure functions are easier to test than components, but the ranking algorithm has many branches (4 fields × N terms × M posts).

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Build search UI components (island, excerpt, query sync)
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break this task into six subtasks: (1) Update PostCard to accept optional excerpt ReactNode prop and render it in the card body after description, (2) Create SearchExcerpt client component reading query/index from context, rendering null when no query/no body match, or rendering excerpt with <mark> highlights, (3) Create BlogSearch island with search input, query state, lazy index loading (on focus or ?q= mount), React context providing { query, index, indexStatus }, and rendering logic (no query → original listing, query → ranked results), (4) Implement QuerySync (Suspense-wrapped client component using useSearchParams to read ?q= and push to island state), (5) Update blog/page.tsx to map BlogPostSummaryDTO → SearchablePost, pre-render all PostCards with SearchExcerpt in excerpt slot, build cards Map, wrap in BlogSearch island, (6) Add i18n keys (searchLabel, searchPlaceholder, searchClear, searchResults ICU plural, searchNoResults) and create comprehensive component/integration tests.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This task is very high complexity (9/10) because: (1) BlogSearch is a complex client island managing multiple concerns—query state, lazy index fetch (only on focus or ?q=), context provision, conditional rendering (no query vs results), window.history.replaceState for ?q= (not Next.js router to avoid RSC requests), keyboard handling (Esc clears)—this is the most complex client component in the blog feature, (2) The page.tsx integration is intricate: Server Component fetches BlogPostSummaryDTO[], maps to SearchablePost[] (extracting only { slug, title, description, tags }), pre-renders all PostCards with SearchExcerpt in excerpt slot, builds a Map<slug, ReactNode> of cards, passes everything to BlogSearch island—this is a novel pattern not used elsewhere in the codebase (no other 'islands' wrapping server-rendered content), (3) Browser-bundle hygiene is critical and error-prone: BlogSearch, SearchExcerpt, and search/ utilities must never import from @repo/application; the page (Server Component) is the only place that touches BlogPostSummaryDTO and maps it to SearchablePost, (4) QuerySync requires Suspense wrapper and useSearchParams (async API), adding another layer of client/server coordination, (5) The codebase has 60+ component tests (PostCard.test.tsx, FeaturedPosts.test.tsx) but no existing 'island' pattern to follow—this is architectural innovation, (6) Testing must cover: empty query rendering, typing triggering ranked results, index fetch on focus (once), index fetch on ?q= mount, keyboard (Esc clear), ?q= sync (replaceState), no-results message, SearchablePost vs BlogPostSummaryDTO type safety, (7) i18n requires ICU plural for searchResults, adding another validation step.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: Final integration, build verification, and cross-locale manual testing
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break this task into three subtasks: (1) Run full monorepo checks (pnpm test/lint/types across @repo/application, @repo/utils, site) and verify build output (pnpm --filter site build confirms listing still static, 3 search-index.json files generated, inspect one file for structure/no Markdown syntax), (2) Execute comprehensive manual browser testing across both themes and two locales (en-US, pt-BR) covering all 14 scenarios: title/tag/body search, accent-insensitive matching, multi-word AND logic, no-results flow, back-navigation ?q= persistence, Esc/clear, keyboard navigation, mobile viewport, no-JS fallback, failed index fetch, (3) Verify no regressions (PostCard unchanged elsewhere, no 'use client' importing @repo/application via grep, no 200+ line files, all i18n keys present, no core/infra changes, no new npm deps) and document any edge cases found for follow-up issues.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This task is moderate complexity (5/10) because: (1) It's primarily QA and verification rather than implementation—running existing commands (pnpm test/lint/types/build) following known patterns, (2) The 14-scenario manual test plan is comprehensive but straightforward to execute with clear pass/fail criteria, (3) Regression checks are mechanical (grep for 'use client' imports, file length checks, i18n key presence via messages.test.ts), (4) The task depends on all prior tasks (1-4) completing successfully, so the scope is well-defined with no new code, (5) However, manual browser testing across 2 themes × 2 locales × 14 scenarios = ~56 checks is time-consuming and requires attention to detail (easy to miss edge cases like failed index fetch or mobile viewport issues), (6) The codebase has strong test infrastructure (packages/application has 15 blog tests, packages/utils has 20+ tests, apps/site has 60+ component tests) so automated verification is reliable, (7) Build verification is simple (confirm static output, inspect JSON files) with clear acceptance criteria from PRD §4, (8) The main risk is missing regressions in PostCard usage on other pages (featured, tags, archive) or subtle 'use client' boundary violations, but these are discoverable via automated checks.
